title: Session Sculptor: adaptive turn merging and KV aging for streaming chat
creator: Priya Nair
description: Goal: Reduce tail latency and GPU memory fragmentation for long-lived streaming chat sessions by forming batches that respect session density, token-age, and KV cache locality. The Session Sculptor heuristic composes three signals: inter-turn compactness (how close turns are in time and token count), KV-slot locality (probability that cached KV entries will be reused when a request is placed in the same microbatch), and slab-fit score (expected GPU slab packing improvement). This ticket scopes algorithm design, simulation runs on production traces, an implementation prototype in the microbatch planner, and a conservative rollout with realtime metrics.
acceptance_criteria:
1) New batch formation reduces p99 generation latency under streaming load by >= 10% for representative chat workloads (measured against baseline of current slab batcher).
2) GPU memory fragmentation metric (per-GPU free-slab-count) improves by >= 15% on average across traces with mixed session lengths.
3) KV cache hit-rate for microbatches increases by >= 8% without increasing average latency.
4) No regressions in p50 latency or successful token throughput for high-priority customers.
5) End-to-end tests and canary rollout plan validated in staging.
implementation_notes:
- Add lightweight session density estimator in front of the microbatch planner (O(1) per arrival).
- Maintain rolling token-age histogram per session to compute an urgency score (recent activity boosts merging affinity).
- KV affinity score computed from per-session KV access fingerprint: sessions with overlapping top-K keys get positive affinity.
- Compute combined merge_score = alpha*density + beta*urgency + gamma*kv_affinity + delta*slab_fit. We will tune alphas via grid search on offline traces.
- Integrate a conservative backpressure safeguard: if combined batch spans > configured latency budget, force flush.
- GPU slab packing: prefer merges that reduce inter-slab crossovers; compute estimated slab_delta when considering two candidate turns.
- Implement an approximate fast path: if kv_affinity is high and estimated additional tokens < microbatch_token_cap/4, merge immediately without scheduling optimizer run.
- Ensure trace tags on every decision for postmortem analysis (decision_reason, scores, tokens_merged).
experiments:
Planned experiments on production-sampled traces:
- Sweep alpha/beta/gamma/delta to maximize p99 reduction subject to p50 constraint.
- Compare heuristics to baseline slab-only and to recent session-amalgamator prototypes.
- Run live A/B in staging (10% of traffic) collecting p50/p95/p99, kv_hit_rate, gpu_util, slab_free_count.
- Benchmarks will use three persona traces: short-turn chatbots, long-context assistants, and mixed conversation flows.
Preliminary simulation (on 24k sessions sampled): expected p99 improvement 12% and kv_hit_rate +9% at alpha=0.45,beta=0.25,gamma=0.2,delta=0.1.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for scoring functions and slab_delta estimator.
- Integration test with microbatch planner on synthetic traffic harness to assert flush invariants.
- Staging canary at 10% traffic for 48h, validate no more than 2% increase in errors or client timeouts.
- Load test to validate throughput per GPU meets SLA.
- Regression test that streaming backpressure still forces flush under heavy overload.
rollout_plan:
1) Merge behind feature flag.
2) Run offline simulation and collect metrics.
3) Enable in staging (10% routing) for 48h, evaluate metrics and logs.
4) Gradually increase to 50% then to 100% per region with automated rollback if p99 latency regresses > 5% or error rate increases > 1%.
5) After 2 weeks of stable signals, enable default flag for runtime-2.4.
risks:
- Over-merging could increase head latency for low-latency flows if urgency weighting mis-tuned.
- KV affinity estimation could be noisy for new sessions leading to incorrect merges.
- Slab estimator is approximate; misestimates could create cross-slab churn causing transient memory pressure.
- More complex scoring increases CPU on front-end path; must validate cost vs benefit.
rollback_plan: Toggle feature flag off to revert to current slab batcher. Maintain automatic rollback if any of the alerting thresholds are exceeded during rollout. If memory regressions occur, revert and ship a tightened slab-fit-only heuristic while we diagnose.
